Stoneham Oral History Project: World War I
abstract: 2 sound files (120 minutes), digital, MPEG3 file This interview includes the following topics: Captain Howe is a Stoneham native. He attended the U.S.S. Ranger Nautical school during the war. On January 15, 1919, Captain Howe was on leave, when he witnessed the "Great Molasses Flood" in Boston's North End. Captain Howe is a Navy career person. He also served in WWII and the Korean conflict. It was his privilege to serve on "flag ships" during his service. Originally issued on sound cassettes

title: Fire boat engine 31
abstract: Engine # 31 which was not in the fire house the day of the molasses flood. This boat was instrumental in the clean up of the North End once it was realized that salt water helped to dissolve molasses.

title: Transcript of oral history interview with Sam Gurvitz
abstract: Interview of Sam Gurvitz conducted by unnamed interviewer. Gurvitz describes his family’s emigration from Russia to North America. He discusses the ethnic composition and culture of the North End’s Jewish community. Gurvitz speaks about growing up in the North End, describing his living conditions, educational background, family members, leisure activities, and work experience. He discusses his current involvement with different museums and libraries, listing his contributions and titles. Gurvitz explains fundamental differences between Judaism and Christianity, comparing their beliefs, practices, and places of worship. Gurvitz discusses Jewish traditions and holidays, reflecting on his Passover, Shabbat, and Purim celebrations. He talks about his father’s Kosher restaurant business, his immigration to the North End, and his initial work experiences. Gurvitz discusses his encounters with anti-Semitism and anti-immigrant attitudes during the mid-twentieth century. He describes the Italian, Irish and Jewish sections of the North End, the tensions between these groups, and how the North End’s ethnic makeup has changed over time. Gurvitz discusses the Jewish community’s relationship with the larger Boston community and neighborhood organizations. He concludes the interview by discussing major historical events related to North End and Boston, including the Boston Molasses Flood of1919, the Boston Police Strike of 1919, the origin of the Ponzi scheme, and the Brinks Robbery. title: Oral History Interview with John Devlin
abstract: Interview of John Devlin, conducted by Sari Roboff. Devlin discuss the various immigrant groups and notable Irish immigrants who lived in the North End. He describes the shifts in composition of Irish and and Italian immigrant groups, discusses the Jewish immigrant culture, and reflects on how different immigrant groups interacted in the North End. Devlin talks about discriminations against Irish Catholic immigrants in America and how it has changed in the present day. He also compares political engagement of the past to current political activism. Devlin reflects on growing up in the North End, discussing his living conditions, socioeconomic status, educational background, and leisure activities. He also discusses his family’s experiences before and after immigrating to America, including his father’s work for a gas company and the Boston Public Works Department. Devlin talks about Boston’s background in the medicine field and his own involvement with organizations related to the field. He concludes with his views on the state of health care in Boston, including his personal experience with medical practitioners. Other topics mentioned include Jewish immigration, Swedish immigration, parochial schools, St. Mary, John F. Fitzgerald (Honey Fitz), Miller Candy Corporation, James A. Carney, public bathhouses, Boston Molasses flood, North Bennett Street, the National League, the Yankees, Boston College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Faulkner Hospital, University of Massachusetts, Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH), St. Vincent de Paul Society, North End parades, Joseph Stanislasow, County Donegal, Ireland, Emmanuel College, Spanish American War, Dewey Square, Boston Consolidated Gas Company, Boston Public Works Department, Glen Guard House, Haymarket Relief Station, Beth Israel Hospital.
